key_idea: By Hall's theorem every k-subset of services is matchable iff every service set T with |T|<=k has at least |T| engineers knowing something in T; so the answer is (smallest violating |T|) - 1.
sketch: Count engineers by skill mask, then a sum-over-subsets DP gives sub[X] = number of engineers whose skills are a subset of X. For a service set T, the neighbourhood size is n - sub[complement(T)]. Scan all 2^m sets T, find the minimum popcount with neighbourhood < popcount; answer is that minus 1, or m if none violates. O(m*2^m) time and 2^m memory. Pitfall: it must hold for all sets of size up to k, which is why the minimum violating size is what matters. Verified against brute-force bipartite matching over all subsets for small n,m.
